findings.text: _checkout_head_from_files re-implements the capability reckon/git_head.py:82 _head_identity owns (its module docstring is "Read a checkout's HEAD identity as files, without spawning git") and does it more weakly: it reads repository/.git/HEAD literally, so a linked worktree (whose .git is a file) and a packed ref both resolve to "", which collapses the cache key at :2624 to the index stat identity alone; a cached negative reading can then survive a HEAD move and the notice this node exists to raise is never derived. Importing the owner, or hoisting both readers to it, removes the fork; folding this duplication into a node also answers the same class of finding the previous round raised.

the cached reading has no test that it re-derives after the checkout moves: every case in tests/test_a_landing_leaves_the_index_at_head.py builds a fresh temporary checkout, and the station's steady-state case only proves a tick with nothing moved runs no git, so a cache whose key stopped changing would pass all of them while serving a stale notice or a stale silence. A case that repairs the index in place and reads a second time would redden on that regression.

justifications.scope_discipline: the diff from 5f4590af to ae1a0ca3 touches only reckon/crew/obligations.py, reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py, reckon/velocity.py, tests/test_a_landing_leaves_the_index_at_head.py and the node's own evidence fragment, and the two new modules were granted by resume-2-advice.txt before they were edited.
